entry.name: Using Automated Combat States and Outcomes

pages.name: Quick Start and Apply Outcome
pages.content:
Using Automated Combat States and Outcomes

The action system tracks combat costs and automates persistent states, Item readiness, and successful outcomes. Actions can be launched from Take Action on a Character or NPC sheet or, when relevant, from a Skill's roll dialog.

Starting an Action

  1. Target any affected token before opening the action dialog.
  2. Open Take Action, or click the relevant Skill.
  3. Choose the action, target, and Item requested by the dialog.
  4. Confirm the action and complete any roll.
  5. Push or accept the roll as normal.
  6. If a successful rolled outcome is available, click Apply Outcome on the final chat card.

Immediate and Rolled Automation

  • Immediate actions: prone, standing, cover, aiming, overwatch, bow or grenade preparation, and most inventory-readiness changes apply as soon as the action is confirmed. They do not use Apply Outcome.
  • Rolled outcomes: shove, disarm, grapple, break free, First Aid, Rally, retrieving an Item from a backpack, and extinguishing fire require a successful final roll before Apply Outcome appears.

Apply Outcome is hidden after an unsuccessful roll and after the outcome has already been applied. For blockable actions, only successes remaining after Block count. A player must own the affected Actor; otherwise the GM must apply the outcome.

Action Tracking

In a started Combat, Slow and Fast actions are deducted when the action or roll is confirmed. A Fast Action may use an available Slow Action when no Fast Action remains. Free actions are not deducted. Outside active combat, action costs are narrative.

pages.name: Prone and Standing
pages.content:
Prone and Standing

Drop to the Ground

Drop to the ground is a Free Action. Confirming it immediately adds the Prone status to the acting Character or NPC.

Get Up

Get up is a Fast Action. It is available only while the Actor is Prone and immediately removes the Prone status.

Movement Restrictions

  • Crawl is a Fast Mobility action and requires the Actor to be Prone.
  • Run cannot be used while Prone.
  • Dropping prone, getting up, and crawling are unavailable while the Actor is Swimming or Submerged.

Other Automated Ways to Become Prone

  • A successful Shove outcome makes the target Prone.
  • A successful initial Grapple outcome makes both participants Prone.
  • A successful reactive Drop prone from a grenade outcome makes the Actor Prone before the blast. Resolve the corresponding one-step Blast reduction when choosing the effective Blast rating.

The Prone status is used by other automation. It can provide a stable firing position for Sniper Aim and normally reduces Blast by one step unless the explosive is an Airburst.

pages.name: Partial and Full Cover
pages.content:
Partial and Full Cover

Seeking Cover

Seek partial cover and Seek full cover are Fast Actions. Before opening the action dialog, optionally target the threatening attacker. Then enter the terrain or barrier's Armor Level in the cover dialog.

  • With a targeted attacker, the stored cover applies against that Actor.
  • With no target, the cover is treated as applying in every direction.
  • Partial and Full Cover are mutually exclusive; assuming one removes the other.

Protection

  • Partial Cover: the stored Armor Level protects hits to the torso and legs.
  • Full Cover: the stored Armor Level protects every hit location and qualifying ranged attacks suffer a −3 modifier.

When damage is applied, the stored Armor Level is offered as the cover barrier. The attack source must match the stored direction for directional cover to apply.

Changing Cover

  • Go from full to partial cover: Fast Action; requires Full Cover.
  • Go from partial to full cover: Free Action; requires Partial Cover.

The conversion preserves the previously entered Armor Level and direction while changing which locations are protected.

Losing Cover Through Movement

Run, Crawl, Retreat, crossing a low or high barrier, and moving through a door automatically remove the cover status and stored cover details. Other movement not launched through these actions may require the GM to remove or update cover manually.

pages.name: Aiming and Overwatch
pages.content:
Aiming and Overwatch

Aim

Aim is a Fast Action. Choose the ranged Weapon and optionally a target. The system adds Aiming and records the Weapon and target.

  • An aimed attack with the recorded Weapon and target avoids the normal quick-shot penalty.
  • Without Aim, pistols, carbines, and submachine guns receive −1; other ranged Weapons normally receive −2.
  • Heavy Weapons cannot fire until they have been aimed.
  • If no target was selected while aiming, the first targeted attack with that Weapon binds the aim to that target.

Aim persists while the Actor continues attacking the same target with the same Weapon. Choosing another action, Weapon, or target clears it.

Sniper Aim

Sniper aim is a Slow Action and requires a scoped Weapon. It grants +2 when the shooter has cover, is Prone, or uses a bipod; otherwise it grants +1. Sniper Aim disables ammunition dice for that attack.

Overwatch

Assume overwatch position is a Fast Action. Choose a ranged Weapon and optionally a watched Character. The system adds Overwatch and records the declared Weapon and target.

  • Overwatch allows an attack to be rolled outside the Actor's normal turn.
  • The system does not decide when the declared trigger occurs; the players and GM initiate the attack.
  • Making the attack consumes the Overwatch state.
  • Taking another action also clears Overwatch.

On an urban Scene, Overwatch an aperture records the chosen Weapon and aperture mode. Mark the watched door, window, or breach on the Scene. If simultaneous overwatch fire needs resolution, the free Resolve simultaneous overwatch fire Ranged Combat action is available.

pages.name: Bow and Grenade Preparation
pages.content:
Bow and Grenade Preparation

Prepare Bow

Prepare bow is a Fast Action. Select an ordinary Bow Weapon. The system marks that Item as prepared, and an unprepared Bow is prevented from firing.

  • Firing the Bow consumes its prepared state.
  • Preparing, aiming, or shooting the Bow preserves the preparation while the sequence continues.
  • Choosing another action clears prepared ordinary Bows.
  • Crossbows are excluded from this preparation requirement.

Pull Grenade Pin

Pull grenade pin is a Fast Action. Select the Grenade Item. The system marks that specific Item as prepared, and an unprepared Grenade is prevented from being thrown.

  • The prepared state remains on that Grenade until it is thrown or changed manually.
  • Throwing the Grenade consumes its prepared state.
  • Preparation does not itself reduce Item Quantity; normal attack resolution handles disposable Item consumption when ammunition tracking is enabled.

Choosing the Correct Item

The action launcher filters the Item menu. Prepare Bow accepts Weapons whose Type identifies them as a bow but not a crossbow. Pull Grenade Pin accepts Grenade Items. If an expected Item is missing, check its Item type, Weapon Type field, and that it belongs to the acting Actor.

pages.name: Inventory Readiness
pages.content:
Inventory Readiness

Physical Items use Equipped and Stored in the backpack to determine which readiness actions can select them.

Get Item from Backpack

This is a Slow Mobility action. Select an Item currently stored in the backpack. After a successful final roll, click Apply Outcome:

  • Stored in the backpack is cleared.
  • The Item remains unequipped.
  • A separate Draw Item action is normally needed before it is ready in hand.

Draw Item from Combat Gear

This is a Fast Action with no roll. Select a physical Item that is not in the backpack. Confirming the action immediately marks it Equipped and ensures it is not stored in the backpack.

Drop Held Item

This is a Free Action with no roll. Select an equipped Weapon, Gear Item, or Grenade. Confirming the action clears Equipped. It does not remove the Item from the Actor or create an Item on the Scene.

Drop Backpack

This is a Fast Action that records that the Actor has dropped their backpack. It removes the carried-backpack penalty from supported water actions, but does not delete or individually move the Items marked as backpack contents. Recovering the backpack or changing those Item locations remains a manual inventory task.

Readiness and Other Workflows

Disarm only offers equipped Weapons, Gear, and Grenades. Reloading from backpack ammunition has its own retrieval check. Manually editing Equipped or Stored in the backpack remains available when the fiction does not require a tracked combat action.

pages.name: Shove and Disarm
pages.content:
Shove and Disarm

Both actions are Fast Close Combat tests against another targeted Character or NPC. They are blockable: the target's owner or GM first chooses Block or Do Not Block, and Block successes cancel action successes before the outcome is evaluated.

Shove

  1. Target the opponent.
  2. Choose Shove and complete the attack and any Block.
  3. Push or accept the roll.
  4. Click Apply Outcome if enough effective successes remain.
  • Normally one success is required.
  • If the target's Strength is greater than the attacker's Strength, two successes are required.
  • A successful outcome makes the target Prone.
  • It also clears the target's stored close-quarters engagement, where applicable.

Disarm

  1. Target the opponent and choose Disarm.
  2. Resolve the attack, any Block, and any Push.
  3. Click Apply Outcome.
  4. If several eligible equipped Items exist, choose which one is disarmed.
  • One success is required for a one-handed Item.
  • Two successes are required for an Item marked Two-Handed.
  • The chosen Weapon, Gear Item, or Grenade has Equipped cleared.

Disarm does not transfer the Item, delete it, or place it on the Scene. The Item remains in the target's inventory.

pages.name: Grapple and Break Free
pages.content:
Grapple and Break Free

Starting a Grapple

Grapple is a Slow Close Combat action against another Character or NPC. The initial attempt can be Blocked.

  1. Target the opponent and choose Grapple.
  2. Resolve any Block, then accept or push the roll.
  3. With at least one effective success, click Apply Outcome.

The automated outcome:

  • Makes the grappler Prone.
  • Makes the target Prone and Restrained.
  • Records both sides of the grapple relationship.

Restrictions While Grappling

  • The restrained target can only choose Break free.
  • The grappler can only choose Grapple attack.
  • Grapple Attack must target the recorded opponent.

Grapple Attack is a Fast Close Combat roll. On land, any damage or additional narrative effect still requires normal GM resolution. In water, its Apply Outcome can submerge the target and initiate the supported hold-breath and drowning checks.

Break Free

Break free is a Slow Close Combat action available only to an Actor recorded as grappled. After a successful final roll, Apply Outcome removes Restrained and clears the stored grapple relationship on both participants where document permissions allow.

If one side remains stuck because the player does not own the counterpart Actor, ask the GM to apply the outcome or clear the remaining status and relationship.

pages.name: First Aid and Rally
pages.content:
First Aid and Rally

Both are Slow support actions against another targeted Character or NPC. A successful outcome restores capacity equal to the final number of successes, capped at the target's maximum.

First Aid

  • Uses the world-configured First Aid Skill, with Medical Aid as the fallback.
  • The target must be incapacitated by damage: current Health must be zero.
  • A suitable medical Gear Item is optional. The launcher recognises Gear named or typed as medical, medkit, surgical, or first aid equipment.
  • Apply Outcome restores one Health per success.

The system records who has attempted treatment during the current incapacitation. Without a selected medical Item, the same caregiver cannot try again until a successful outcome clears the attempt history. Selecting suitable medical Gear permits another attempt.

Rally

  • Uses the world-configured Rally Skill, with Command as the fallback.
  • The target must be incapacitated by stress: current Stress Capacity must be zero.
  • Apply Outcome restores one Stress Capacity per success.

Each character may attempt Rally once during the target's current stress incapacitation. A successful outcome clears the recorded attempt history.

Applying the Result

The attempt is recorded when the roll is made, including an unsuccessful attempt. Push or accept the roll first. Apply Outcome appears only after a successful final result and changes the target only once.

pages.name: Extinguishing Fire and Troubleshooting
pages.content:
Extinguishing Fire

Extinguish fire is a Slow Mobility action. It can target the acting Actor or another targeted Actor, including a Vehicle carrying the Fire status.

  1. For another Actor, target their token before opening the action dialog. With no target selected, the action applies to self.
  2. Choose Extinguish Fire and make the configured Skill test.
  3. Push or accept the roll.
  4. After a successful final result, click Apply Outcome.

The target must already have the Fire status. Apply Outcome removes Fire. An unsuccessful roll leaves the status in place.

World Skill Configuration

Open Game Settings → Configure Settings → System Settings → Action Skills to map the world's Skill Items for Shove, Disarm, Grapple, Break Free, First Aid, Rally, Get Item from Backpack, and Extinguish Fire. Every acting Character needs an embedded copy of the configured Skill.

If Apply Outcome Is Missing

  • Finish all Push and Block resolution first.
  • The final roll must have at least one effective success.
  • Some outcomes require additional successes: Shove against a stronger target and Disarm against a Two-Handed Item require two.
  • Immediate state actions never show Apply Outcome because they have already changed the Actor or Item.

If Apply Outcome Fails

  • The current user must own the affected Actor, or the GM must click it.
  • The original Actor, target, and selected Item must still exist.
  • Check prerequisites: incapacitated Health for First Aid, incapacitated Stress Capacity for Rally, Fire for Extinguish Fire, or an active grapple for Break Free.
  • A previously applied outcome cannot be applied twice.

Manual Corrections

The GM can remove a status effect, edit Item readiness, or adjust Health and Stress Capacity directly when a narrative exception requires it. Use manual changes carefully because stored Aim, Cover, Overwatch, and Grapple relationships may include flags in addition to visible status icons.
